Thanks — great questions. Short answers here and Dev will expand on the Monday call.

1) Embedding cost control
- We can run smaller-dimension embeddings (256-d) for initial experiments; SDK supports selecting embedding encoders.
- Sample-mode: you can index a subset of documents for quality checks, or use caching for repeat queries.
- We also support batching and async embeddings to reduce per-call overhead.

2) Auth options for staging/POC
- Short-lived API tokens: Redwood issues short-lived keys (TTL configurable) — recommended for CI/staging.
- SSO / OIDC integration + short-lived service tokens can be set up for enterprise.
- For private deployments: mutual TLS + customer-managed KMS for key wrapping (recommended for production).

3) Reranker guidance
- Light reranker (distil-cross) for <50ms rerank on CPU for small K; medium cross-encoders on GPU for higher quality (100-200ms).
- If you need sub-100ms end-to-end, dedicated capacity helps and we can quantify with a small benchmark.

Yes — Monday 2026-08-24 10:00 AM PT works for us. Dev will share an agenda and an architecture slide beforehand.

I'll loop in an architecture note in a sec — attaching a slightly updated integration diagram.

—Marissa

Hi Aisha / Marissa — quick technical summary and starter snippets to make the Monday sync efficient.

Auth & local env
- For quickstart: set REDWOOD_API_KEY in your environment. Example: export REDWOOD_API_KEY=sk_test_xxx
- For staging without long-lived keys: we can provision a short-lived token via our console or support OIDC with automatic rotation.

Python quickstart (embeddings + rerank flow):

# example steps (plain text in email)
1) pip install redwood-sdk
2) export REDWOOD_API_KEY=...
3) python examples/embeddings_pipeline.py

embeddings_pipeline.py (high level)
from redwood import RedwoodClient
client = RedwoodClient()
# create embeddings for documents
docs = ["doc1 text...", "doc2 text..."]
embs = client.embeddings.create(model="rw-embed-512", inputs=docs)
# index embs into FAISS (local) -> retrieve top_k -> then call reranker
queries = ["How do I update billing?"]
q_embs = client.embeddings.create(model="rw-embed-512", inputs=queries)
# retrieve top-k from local ANN index, then:
rerank = client.rerank.score(model="rw-rerank-small", query=queries[0], candidates=["candidate text..."])

TypeScript quickstart (same flow):
1) npm install @redwood/inference
2) export REDWOOD_API_KEY=...
3) node examples/embeddings_pipeline.ts

// embeddings_pipeline.ts (high level)
import { Redwood } from '@redwood/inference'
const client = new Redwood({ apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY })
const embs = await client.embeddings.create({ model: 'rw-embed-512', input: ['doc1', 'doc2'] })
// store in local Annoy/FAISS -> query -> rerank with client.rerank.score(...)

Local testing tips
- Use the attached sample-apps.md to run the demo UI locally (React app + local FAISS index).
- Docker: included docker-compose stub spins up a small FAISS service + demo frontend.
- Performance: run small load with ab/hey to measure P95; try the quantized model variants for cost/latency tradeoffs.
